pure-announcement.rationale: This is a vendor-authored essay articulating an architectural distinction (one vs. many sources of telemetry truth), not a launch or release note for any product.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (MCP governance, SIEM gaps, context layer, evals) covers the observability 1.0 vs 2.0 storage-model distinction.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The central claim is a checkable technical property — count how many places your telemetry is stored — and the piece links primary sources like Scuba and canonical-log write-ups.

durability.rationale: The core mechanism — wide structured events as a single store with read-time aggregation versus pillar tools that force write-time decisions — is an architectural trade-off that will hold regardless of which vendors survive, though the adoption predictions around it will date.

actionability.rationale: It gives a concrete evaluation test ('how many times is your data stored?') and a design prescription (compose wide canonical events per unit of work, decide at read time) that directly changes instrumentation and tool-selection decisions.

atomicity.rationale: The whole essay reduces to one statable idea — the generational difference is single vs. many sources of truth, and everything else is consequence — which fits in one paragraph independent of Honeycomb's framing.
